page: Microsoft Azure E96ps_v6 is an arm64-based virtual machine belonging to the Epsv6 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is powered by 96 dedicated physical cores of Microsoft's ARM Neoverse-N2 processor operating at a clock speed of 3.4 GHz. The processor architecture features a 1:1 thread-to-core ratio, meaning there is no simultaneous multithreading. Cache specifications include 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 128 MB of L3 cache. The server is equipped with 672.0 GB of system memory, which yields 7.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include any local storage or GPUs, though it is Premium Storage capable.

In benchmark evaluations, the E96ps_v6 demonstrates top-tier multi-core and memory performance. Multi-core metrics from stress-ng, Geekbench, and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression all rank in the top 10% of tested servers. Memory bandwidth is also highly efficient, with both read and write large-block tests placing in the top 10% tier. Conversely, single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the middle 50% average. Cryptographic capabilities are supported via hardware-accelerated AES, though other advanced vector and matrix extensions are absent.

This server configuration is highly suited for memory-intensive and highly parallelized workloads. It achieves top-tier results in Passmark database operations and Redis SET operations, making it an excellent fit for relational and in-memory databases. It is also well-suited for software compilation and static web serving. The ARM-based architecture offers a resource-dense hardware profile, providing qualitative cost efficiency for scale-out workloads that benefit from dedicated physical cores and high memory capacity without requiring x86 instruction sets.
